bottom_line: Compared with placebo, dabigatran was associated with a dose-dependent increase in major or clinically relevant minor bleeding, with hazard ratio (HR) 1.77 (95% confidence intervals 0.70, 4.50) for 50 mg; HR 2.17 (0.88, 5.31) for 75 mg; HR 3.92 (1.72, 8.95) for 110 mg; and HR 4.27 (1.86, 9.81) for 150 mg.
implications: These phase II data show a clear dose-related increase in the primary bleeding composite (e.g., 2.2% placebo vs 7.9% and 7.8% with 110 mg and 150 mg; HR 3.92 [1.72, 8.95] and 4.27 [1.86, 9.81]) alongside reductions in D-dimer (about 37% and 45% lower at Weeks 1 and 4 vs placebo; P , 0.001). The reported ischaemic event rates were low with only numerical differences between groups (3.8% placebo vs 3.0–4.9% dabigatran doses for cardiovascular death/non-fatal MI/non-haemorrhagic stroke), so the document does not establish a statistically proven reduction in clinical ischaemic events, and it states net clinical benefit requires a larger phase III trial.
